rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each proposed module hides substantial behaviour behind a small surface: `imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py` exposes one batch-fetch entry over ssh transport + encode/decode + partial-batch refusals, `imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py` one converter entry over three deck grammars into five IDS netCDF, `imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py` one `export_tokamap_directory` callable over group-scoping and unit/sign/COCOS collapse, and the §7 EQDB reader is declared as one remote script reusing the §3 transport rather than a second path.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the only same-mechanism duplication is the §3 ssh extractor against `imas_codex/remote/` (`executor.py`, `ssh_worker.py`, `serialization.py`), and the plan names that owner and the file, states the reason it does not extend it (importing the codex distribution onto ambix's runtime path drags `neo4j`, `fastmcp`, `rapidfuzz`, `lxml`, `pypdf`), discloses that this is a second transport rather than an extension of the FAIR-MAST mirror (`imas_ambix/data/manifest.py`, `imas_ambix/data/cli.py`), and defers a shared core to the second facility that needs remote execution. Every intra-repo duplicate the item targets — path resolution (`imas_ambix/data/paths.py`), store addressing, the shot registry (`imas_ambix/spine_bench/shots.py`), the COCOS scorer, the equilibrium comparator and the machine-description resolver — is extended at its named owner, not forked.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds surface accounts for it in its own text: §2 exporter "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §3 extractor "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today" and "adds no `ambix data` command"; §4 converter "retires nothing inside ambix, because ambix has no deck reader today", the two store-addressing keys "retire nothing, because the catalogue had no addressing slot" while the probe-angle key "retires the machine branch" in `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py` `read_geometry_table`; §6 moves the hard-coded DIII-D eligibility constants into each loader's declaration; §7's machine-keyed pin table replaces the single `PINNED_SEMANTIC_IDENTITY`/`PINNED_PHYSICAL_DIGEST`/`PINNED_REGISTRY_DIGEST` constants and its two record fields "retire nothing, because no scalar reference comparison exists yet".
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the existing mechanism it extends for every proposal (imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py `load_packaged_signal_map`; imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py `score_convention`/`surviving_conventions`/`format_sign_report`; imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py `measure_diiid_convention` with `_integrated_current`; imas_ambix/challenge/loader.py `load_shot`/`ChallengeShot; imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py `judge_geometry`; imas_ambix/spine_bench/runner.py `_magnetics_residual`; imas_ambix/spine_bench/shots.py `BenchShot`/`resolve_shotset_version`; imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py `resolve_machine_description`; imas_ambix/gs/machine_selection.py `ArtifactMachineSelector.select`), and every one of those symbols exists in the tree at base 4bb5347d.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the sections that layer over existing machinery each state why the owner cannot be extended: §2 keeps the exporter out of the loaders because the loaders must not learn tokamap; §4 widens `StoreEngine.open` rather than adding an engine because a static description has no per-shot cost; §6 generalises `measure_diiid_convention` through a record contract with the DIII-D corpus as first loader rather than a second scorer; §7 routes to `efit_referee.judge_geometry` and reads `_magnetics_residual` from the stamp rather than adding parallel comparators; §3's own extractor is the one deliberate new layer and it declares its owner and reason (see duplicate_owner).
